title: Compatible open chart gluing of local universal thickenings
statement: Let $h:Z\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $C$ a universe-small open cover of $Z$, and $i_k:C_k\to Z'_k$, $h'_k:Z'_k\to X$ universal first order thickenings of $C.f_k$ followed by $h$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening]. There exist a scheme $W$ and open immersions $e_k:Z'_k\to W$ [def-weil-open-immersion] whose images cover $W$, such that (1) the maps $h'_k$ agree on the categorical pullbacks of $e_k$ and $e_l$; (2) the maps $e_k\circ i_k$ agree on the categorical pullbacks of $C.f_k$ and $C.f_l$; and (3) for every $k,l$ and point $z\in C_l$, $e_l(i_l(z))$ lies in the image of $e_k$ if and only if $C.f_l(z)$ lies in the image of $C.f_k$. No global morphism from $Z$, global morphism to $X$, or cartesian square is asserted.

source.place: Tag 04F3, proof: the two paragraphs beginning Choose an affine open covering and By the general remarks; verified at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04F3

proof.text: Take the pullback intersections of source charts. Each first order thickening is a homeomorphism: its closed image is the support of its kernel, which equals the support of its square-zero power and hence is all of the target. The open-pieces theorem supplies the unique corresponding open in each thickened chart and universality of its restriction over the whole base X.

Identify the two sources of each restricted thickening with the source intersection. Universal uniqueness gives the transition isomorphism over X fixing this intersection. On triple intersections uniqueness identifies the composite transition with the direct transition. Repeated indices and reversed pairs similarly give the identity and inverse transitions.

Apply scheme gluing to these overlap opens and transitions. Its canonical open chart maps e_k cover the glued scheme W, and the gluing pullback description identifies their pairwise intersections with the prescribed overlap opens. The transitions are over X, so the h prime maps agree on these pullbacks. They fix source intersections, so i_k followed by e_k agree on the source pullbacks. By construction the inverse image of the overlap open under i_l is the inverse image of the range of C.f_k under C.f_l; the gluing intersection description gives precisely the last pointwise equivalence. Empty covers give the empty scheme.

theorem universalFirstOrderThickening_cartesianAtlas_core
    {Z X : Scheme.{u}} (h : Z ⟶ X) (C : Z.OpenCover.{u})
    (Z' : C.I₀ → Scheme.{u}) (i : ∀ k, C.X k ⟶ Z' k)
    (h' : ∀ k, Z' k ⟶ X)
    (H : ∀ k, IsUniversalFirstOrderThickening (C.f k ≫ h) (i k) (h' k)) :
    ∃ (W : Scheme.{u}) (e : ∀ k, Z' k ⟶ W),
      (∀ k, IsOpenImmersion (e k)) ∧ (∀ w : W, ∃ k z, e k z = w) ∧
      (∀ k l, pullback.fst (e k) (e l) ≫ h' k = pullback.snd _ _ ≫ h' l) ∧
      (∀ k l, pullback.fst (C.f k) (C.f l) ≫ (i k ≫ e k) =
        pullback.snd _ _ ≫ (i l ≫ e l)) ∧
      ∀ k l (z : C.X l),
        e l (i l z) ∈ Set.range (e k) ↔ C.f l z ∈ Set.range (C.f k)
